newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA, ratings agencies will like budget - Costello.
newsitem.headline: RBA, ratings agencies will like budget - Costello.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) and the ratings agencies would like the Australian budget for 1997/98 (July-June), Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday.

Costello said the planned return to an underlying surplus in 1998/99 of A$1.6 billion showed Australia was doing better than the rest of the industrialised world, including the United States, Japan and Europe.
Costello made no comment on interest rates.
"This is a very good effort by world standards," Costello told a news conference during the pre-budget speech lock-up.
He said the Reserve Bank would be very happy with the budget, which forecasts an underlying deficit of A$3.9 billion in 1997/98.
"The Reserve would want to see that the government is putting in place the fiscal measures that it has and I think that they'll be pretty impressed by it," he said.
He said the ratings agencies would look at the debt position, where the budget forecast government debt to GDP to fall from 19 percent in 1995/96 to under 10.5 percent in the year to June 30, 2001.
"In 1996/97, we stabilised debt and we started repaying it. We take Commonwealth debt from about A$100 billion to under A$70 billion by the year 2000," he said.
